sets.name: Licence agreement
sets.engagement: Due diligence review of material contracts for a potential acquisition of Allied Esports Entertainment, Inc.

items.name: Additional Provisions attachment to the Joint Content License Agreement
items.what_it_is: The exhibit containing definitions and supplementary terms incorporated by reference in the agreement.
items.why_needed: The agreement states definitions are set forth in the Additional Provisions; without it key terms are undefined.

items.name: Signature pages / execution copy of the Joint Content License Agreement
items.what_it_is: The final signed pages showing the parties' authorized representatives and dates of execution.
items.why_needed: To confirm the agreement was validly executed and binding on the parties.

items.name: Board of Directors resolution authorizing WPT to enter the agreement
items.what_it_is: Corporate resolution approving the content license agreement and delegating authority to sign.
items.why_needed: Required to verify WPT had proper internal authority to bind itself under the agreement.

items.name: Organizational chart of WPT and its affiliates (including Zynga entities)
items.what_it_is: Diagram showing parent‑subsidiary relationships and affiliate entities referenced in the agreement.
items.why_needed: The agreement defines 'Zynga' to include affiliates; the chart clarifies which entities are bound.

items.name: Schedule of all material contracts of Allied Esports Entertainment
items.what_it_is: List of significant agreements (licenses, partnerships, debt, etc.) to which the company is a party.
items.why_needed: To assess cumulative obligations, exclusivity conflicts, and change‑of‑control provisions.

items.name: Most recent audited financial statements of Allied Esports Entertainment
items.what_it_is: Balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, and accompanying notes audited by an independent CPA.
items.why_needed: Needed to evaluate the financial impact of the license agreement and overall company health.

items.name: Federal and state tax returns for the last three years
items.what_it_is: Completed corporate tax returns (Form 1120, state equivalents) and related schedules.
items.why_needed: To identify tax liabilities, credits, and any positions that could affect post‑closing value.

items.name: Litigation, claims, and contingent liability schedule
items.what_it_is: Summary of pending or threatened lawsuits, arbitrations, regulatory investigations, and indemnities.
items.why_needed: To assess risks that could affect the value or enforceability of the licensed content.

items.name: Intellectual property register (including ZYNGA POKER® trademarks)
items.what_it_is: Catalog of owned and licensed patents, trademarks, copyrights, and domain names with status and renewal dates.
items.why_needed: To verify that the IP underlying the licensed game is properly protected and enforceable.

items.name: Complete SEC filings (8‑K, 10‑Q, 10‑K) referencing the agreement
items.what_it_is: The full periodic reports where the agreement is disclosed as an exhibit or described in MD&A.
items.why_needed: To confirm public disclosure compliance and see any additional context or amendments reported.

sets.name: Endorsement agreement

items.name: Complete, unredacted Endorsement Agreement (Exhibit 10.17)

items.why_needed: To assess total financial exposure and compliance with disclosure requirements.

items.name: Confidential Treatment Request filing with the SEC
items.what_it_is: The letter and supporting documents requesting confidential treatment for redacted portions.
items.why_needed: To verify legitimacy of redactions and ensure no material information is improperly hidden.
items.note: A section with a similar heading exists in ADAMSGOLFINC_03_21_2005-EX-10.17-ENDORSEMENT AGREEMENT.txt: "CONFIDENTIAL TREATMENT REQUESTED". Check whether it is what is needed.

items.name: Board of Directors approval or minutes authorizing the agreement
items.what_it_is: Corporate resolution or meeting minutes showing Adams Golf’s board endorsed the deal.
items.why_needed: Confirms proper corporate authority and avoids claims of ultra vires.

items.name: Executed signature page of the Endorsement Agreement
items.what_it_is: Page bearing signatures of Tom Watson and Adams Golf representative with dates.
items.why_needed: Validates that the agreement is enforceable and not merely a draft.

items.name: Underlying SEC filing (e.g., Form 10-K or 8-K) where Exhibit 10.17 is attached
items.what_it_is: The periodic report containing the exhibit index and contextual disclosures.
items.why_needed: Places the contract in the company’s reporting obligations and assesses materiality.

items.name: Adams Golf’s audited financial statements for the fiscal year covering the agreement
items.what_it_is: Balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement and notes for the relevant year.
items.why_needed: To evaluate the financial impact of compensation and performance bonuses.
items.note: A section with a similar heading exists in ADAMSGOLFINC_03_21_2005-EX-10.17-ENDORSEMENT AGREEMENT.txt: "ADAMS GOLF'S OBLIGATIONS". Check whether it is what is needed.

items.name: Any amendments, waivers, or side letters to the Endorsement Agreement post‑2005
items.what_it_is: Written modifications extending term, altering compensation, or adding obligations.
items.why_needed: Ensures the current obligations reflect the parties’ latest understanding.

items.name: Related‑party disclosure and conflict‑of‑interest policy applicable to Adams Golf
items.what_it_is: Corporate governance document outlining how endorsements with individuals are reviewed.
items.why_needed: Checks whether the agreement was properly vetted for conflicts.

items.name: Insurance or indemnity coverage documents for Adams Golf’s obligations under Sections 14 & 21
items.what_it_is: Policies or self‑insurance arrangements covering indemnity payments to Watson.
items.why_needed: Assesses ability to satisfy indemnity liabilities if triggered.

items.name: Trademark and licensing verification for Adams Golf’s golf clubs referenced in the agreement
items.what_it_is: USPTO registrations or license agreements showing Adams Golf’s rights to the clubs.
items.why_needed: Confirms the company can lawfully grant the endorsement rights contemplated.

sets.name: Services agreement
sets.engagement: Due diligence review of a services agreement between Provider and Recipients (Telcostar Pte Ltd and Ability Computer & Software Industries Ltd) to assess contractual obligations, performance, and risk.

items.name: Services Agreement (core document)
items.what_it_is: The main agreement governing services between Provider and Recipients.
items.why_needed: Baseline for all obligations and rights.
items.evidence: SERVICES AGREEMENT This Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into on October 1, 2019 and is made effective as of November 1, 2019 (the "Effective Date"), by and between [ * * * ] (the "Provider"), and TELCOSTAR PTE, LTD., a company organized and existing under the laws of Singapore and Ability Computer & Software Industries Ltd, a company organized and existing under the laws of the State of Israel (each and both of them "Recipient").

items.name: Exhibit A – Service Description
items.what_it_is: Schedule detailing the specific services, deliverables, timelines, and performance metrics to be provided under the agreement.
items.why_needed: To verify scope of services matches business needs and assess performance obligations.

items.name: Amendment and Waiver Log
items.what_it_is: Record of any amendments, waivers, or side letters to the Services Agreement since its effective date.
items.why_needed: To understand changes that may affect obligations, fees, or termination rights.

items.name: Invoice and Payment Records
items.what_it_is: Billing statements and proof of payment for services rendered under the agreement.
items.why_needed: To confirm compliance with payment terms and identify any arrears or overcharges.

items.name: Insurance Certificates
items.what_it_is: Certificates of liability, cyber, and professional indemnity insurance held by the Provider.
items.why_needed: To ensure adequate coverage for risks arising from service delivery.

items.name: Data Protection / Privacy Compliance Documentation
items.what_it_is: Evidence of compliance with GDPR, PDPA, or other relevant data protection laws (e.g., DPA, privacy impact assessment).
items.why_needed: Because the agreement likely involves processing personal or confidential data.

items.name: Provider’s Audited Financial Statements (last 2 years)
items.what_it_is: Audited balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, and notes for the Provider.
items.why_needed: To assess Provider’s financial capacity to perform services and meet obligations.

items.name: Conflict of Interest Disclosures
items.what_it_is: Statements from Provider and Recipients disclosing any relationships that could create a conflict.
items.why_needed: To evaluate potential bias or breach of exclusivity clauses.

items.name: Regulatory Approvals or Licenses
items.what_it_is: Any government or industry licenses required for the Provider to deliver the services (e.g., telecom, software export).
items.why_needed: To verify legality of service provision under applicable jurisdictions.

sets.name: SEC enforcement order
sets.engagement: Review of SEC administrative settlement concerning Latch, Inc.'s revenue recognition violations under ASC 606 to assess financial, legal, and remedial implications.

items.name: Offer of Settlement
items.what_it_is: The settlement offer submitted by Latch to the SEC resolving the cease‑and‑desist proceeding.
items.why_needed: To determine monetary penalties, injunctive terms, and any admission‑equivalent obligations.

items.name: Internal Investigation and Restatement Report
items.what_it_is: Report of Latch's internal review and the resulting restatement of financials due to revenue recognition errors.
items.why_needed: To quantify the misstatement and evaluate adequacy of remedial actions.
items.note: A section with a similar heading exists in sec-order-latch.txt: "Respondent’s Internal Investigation and Restatement". Check whether it is what is needed.

items.name: Restated Financial Statements
items.what_it_is: Revised GAAP financial statements (e.g., 10‑K/10‑Q) reflecting corrected revenue recognition.
items.why_needed: To assess impact on liquidity, leverage, and compliance with covenants.

items.name: Auditor's Report on Restated Financials
items.what_it_is: Independent auditor's opinion on the restated financial statements.
items.why_needed: To verify reliability of the corrected numbers and identify any audit‑related issues.

items.name: ASC 606 Revenue Recognition Policy Documentation
items.what_it_is: Latch's formal accounting policy memorandum describing its ASC 606 application.
items.why_needed: To evaluate whether the policy was properly designed and applied prior to the violation.
items.note: A section with a similar heading exists in sec-order-latch.txt: "1. These proceedings arise out of revenue recognition errors by Respondent, a". Check whether it is what is needed.

items.name: SEC‑Latch Correspondence File
items.what_it_is: Letters, emails, and meeting minutes exchanged between Latch and SEC staff regarding the proceeding.
items.why_needed: To understand negotiation dynamics, any factual admissions, and procedural history.

items.name: Form 8‑K Disclosure of Settlement
items.what_it_is: Company's current report announcing the SEC settlement and its terms.
items.why_needed: To gauge market disclosure adequacy and potential reputational effect.

items.name: Board Minutes Approving Settlement
items.what_it_is: Excerpt of board of directors' meeting minutes where the settlement was authorized.
items.why_needed: To confirm governance oversight and authorization of the remedial agreement.
